newsitem.title: UK: Rapid Asia power growth sparks finance innovations.
newsitem.headline: Rapid Asia power growth sparks finance innovations.

text.p: Surging electricity demand in Asia is encouraging western finance houses to explore new ways of financing independent power projects (IPPs) in developing countries, a leading banker said on Tuesday.

Electricity demand in India, for example, has increased at a rapid nine percent per annum over the past few years, and the country can expect a 22 percent shortfall in power supply by the year 2000, Gordon Branston, head of Global Structured Finance at ANZ investment bank told in industry conference in London.
"The need for power in Asia is quite obvious," he said.
Thirteen new Asian IPPs, representing 2,900 megawatts (MW) of supply, should have financing in place by spring 1999, he said.
The power sector dominates the Asia-Pacific project finance business, pulling in 55 percent of total project investment in 1995.
While IPPs have been traditionally financed by syndicated loans, bankers are now testing the waters of capital markets to raise capital.
"(Capital market financing) will increasingly come into play in the future, but it will take just one project to go off the tracks for the market to dry up," Branston said.

The bureaucratic and political problems surrounding U.S. gas company Enron Corp's $2.3 billion, 2,450 MG gas-fired power project in Dabhol in the Indian sate of Maharashtra sent jitters through financial markets, but their successful resolution restored confidence, he said.
"Today it is seen as a positive outcome -- a catalyst for restored confidence in the power sector in India," Branston said.
Work on the power plant resumed late last year after the ruling Hindu nationalist government renegotiated a contract it had said was too expensive in terms of tariffs.
Branston said that efforts to revise electricity tariff structures in Asia should hearten financiers.

"Demand for both power and financing is clearly there...supply in terms of debt financing is there, and we should see some increase in sophistication with the growth of capital market solutions," he said.
